responsibility: Contains the main procedural implementation of the RISC-V GCC backend. This is the target’s central code-generation file: it defines core backend data structures such as frame, argument, and address classification records; implements register, calling-convention, frame-layout, constant/address legitimization, cost-model, section/assembly-output, varargs, attribute, thunk, sibling-call, and reorg logic; and binds those routines to GCC through the large set of `TARGET_*` hook definitions and the final `struct gcc_target targetm = TARGET_INITIALIZER`, making it the primary executable counterpart to the declarative configuration in `riscv.h`, `riscv.opt`, and `riscv.md`.
same_name_distinction: Within the `riscv` same-name group, this `.c` file is the executable backend implementation: it defines the target-side data structures and functions for code generation, calling conventions, frame handling, address/constant legalization, builtins, asm output, and machine reorg, and connects them through many `TARGET_*` hooks and `struct gcc_target targetm = TARGET_INITIALIZER`. Unlike `riscv.h`, it is not the macro/declaration interface; unlike `riscv.md`, it is not the RTL pattern description; and unlike `riscv.opt`, it is not the option table that drives `-m` parsing and target variables.
